description: Found by the fz-go4.37 re-audit (2026-07-03, confirmed pre-existing — reproduced at parent dc26bf0b0, NOT caused by fz-go4.37). fixtures2/00277_enum_tier0_fixture.fz (builds %{2=>:two,1=>:one} and calls Enum.member?/reduce/count/to_list over it) engages max 5 return-type ascents, exceeding the pinned budget of <=4 that sweep_corpus_for_return_widening asserts (drive_test.rs:~10846). It is SCHEDULE-DEPENDENT (parent showed max 4 on one run, max 5 on three repeats) — consistent with the known non-monotone Seal<->DeriveRuntimeDemand<->Transport convergence issue (project_fz_f98_convergence_runaway). Currently MASKED because 00277's home shard (index%4 in {0,1,3}) is #[ignore = red-worklist]; only shard_2 is active. TASK: this is the return-widening-over-budget symptom of the broader ReturnType-fixpoint nondeterminism (relate to fz-go4.18.28.6). Diagnose whether 00277's 5th ascent is genuine work or the convergence wobble; either bring it under budget or, if it's the .28.6 nondeterminism, fold into that ticket's fix. Do NOT just bump the budget to 5 (that masks the signal). Connect to fz-go4.18.28.6.

comments.text:
DIAGNOSIS (2026-07-04, read-only investigation at 311e70cf1): VERDICT (b) convergence wobble, SAME mechanism as fz-go4.18.28.6 (which already names 00277 as its flagship reproducer). Ascent counter is semantic.rs:681-743 ActivationMap::define_return (increments only on strict change; RETURN_WIDENING_BUDGET=8 internal), emitted at world.rs:769-807 as return_type.defined{ascents}. Distribution over 30 single-binary in-process drives: {5: ~22-27, 6: ~3-8} -- RUN-TO-RUN variance within one binary (scheduler-interleaving level), NOT deterministic-per-binary like 00181 was. Trace of the offending activation (an Enum stdlib activation fn 206, NOT user main): the stored return-type sequence is STRICTLY INCREASING and never re-visits a settled type (e.g. Ty360->396->547->578->698), so it is NOT naive 're-ascend a settled type' wobble. The 5-vs-6 difference is BATCHING GRANULARITY: whether two upstream contributions to fn 206's return land in one wake or two is schedule-dependent (578->698 in one hop vs 582->699->719 in two). Genuine multi-hop stdlib-dispatch depth + schedule-dependent step-counting = the .28.6 non-monotone convergence, not a new root cause. RECOMMENDATION: do NOT pin budget to 5/6 (the settled state itself is unstable per .28.6/fz-go4.24 which notes 00277 gives schedule-dependent WRONG answers too); keep 00277 parked in ignored shard_1 until .28.6's convergence fix lands, then re-run this sweep to re-derive the correct budget once the fixpoint is monotone.

SHARD FACT CORRECTION (verified against drive_test.rs:10853-10869): the ticket text 'index%4 in {0,1,3} ignored, only shard_2 active' is INVERTED. Reality: ONLY shard_1 (fn compiler2_corpus_never_engages_return_widening_shard_1, line 10859) is #[ignore = red-worklist]; shards 0/2/3 are ACTIVE hard gates. 00277 is corpus index 213, 213%4==1 -> shard_1, so it IS masked -- but via shard_1 alone, not {0,1,3}.
